summary.headline: Innova Captab Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR470.9 crores, with EBITDA up 33% to INR75.1 crores at a 16% margin.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 34% YoY to INR470.9 crores, with CDMO at INR328.7 crores (+32%) and branded generics at INR142.2 crores (+39%). EBITDA was INR75.1 crores (16% margin, +33%) and PAT was INR44.1 crores (+42%). Management said volume growth was 20-22% and the rest of growth came from mix and pricing. Jammu turned EBITDA-positive at roughly INR1-1.5 crores on about INR107 crores of quarterly revenue, up from about INR90 crores in the prior quarter.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR328.7 crores, +32% YoY, driven by portfolio expansion, new customers and higher wallet share with existing customers.

segments.name: Branded generics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR142.2 crores, +39% YoY, with focus on deepening presence in existing markets and entering new domestic and international geographies.

segments.name: Jammu plant
segments.commentary: Around INR107 crores revenue in Q1 and positive EBITDA of INR1-1.5 crores; annualised utilisation about 25-30%; asset turn expected north of 3x at optimum.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: 20%+ revenue growth, with profitability growing faster than revenue; management clarified the 20%+ growth refers to volume.
Management said volume growth of 20%+ is expected for FY27 on a year-on-year closing basis, with the Q1 volume growth of 20-22%.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance held at 15-16% +/-2%; management suggested a normalised 17-18% band, with Jammu adding 2-3 pts once mature.
Gross margin expected to stay within +/-2% of about 35.5% for the full year.
Jammu peak revenue estimated at about INR1,400 crores at 65-70% utilisation; management said it could cross INR1,000 crores with new country and product approvals.
Sharon organic business guided to grow in the early teens; Jammu adds the top-up to reach 20%+ overall.
Maintenance capex guided at INR20-25 crores and growth/debottlenecking capex at INR20-30 crores per year for FY27 and FY28; Baddi new plot plan not yet firmed up.
capex_capacity: Jammu plant started ramping up in January of last year; annualised Q1 utilisation about 25-30%; asset turn expected north of 3x at optimum.
Jammu expansion is the INR500 crore project; management said future expansions would come in tranches of about INR200-250 crores, not a single INR1,000 crore outlay.
Jammu has capacity in penem, beta and cephalosporin categories sufficient for the next two to three years.
Future growth capex is for debottlenecking, equipment replacement or doubling equipment capability; any greenfield project would be announced to the market with board approval.
Baddi new plot bought last year; plan not yet firmed up.
demand_pricing: Volume growth was 20-22% YoY at the overall manufacturing level; ex-Jammu volume growth was about 12-14%. The balance of revenue growth came from mix and pricing.
Pricing model is cost-plus with API price pass-through; management said API prices moved upward in the quarter and the company does not speculate on API prices.
Logistics cost rose slightly in the quarter; management said it was not material.
Management said the company is present in six or seven therapeutic categories and will expand both existing capacity and new dosage forms/categories.
R&D spend is about 0.7-1% of revenue.
Semaglutide: batches being worked on by the plant team; development status unchanged from the prior call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jammu capacity utilisation and asset turn?
qa_highlights.answer: Annualised Q1 utilisation is about 25-30%, with asset turn expected above 3x at optimum.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and is it normalising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash conversion cycle is maintained at 90 days +/-10 days at group level, and Jammu working capital was built up in the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin profile sustainable ex-Jammu?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15-16% +/-2% blended guidance; said ex-Jammu margin around 20% is not the steady state and that 17-18% is a fair normalised level.

qa_highlights.question: What are the maintenance and growth capex numbers for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex INR20-25 crores per year; growth capex INR20-30 crores per year for existing capability augmentation and debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Has there been any pricing pressure this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices moved in an upward direction in the quarter, passed through under the cost-plus model.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company see a conflict of interest between CDMO and branded generics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said branded generics are treated as a normal CDMO customer by plants, with arm's-length transfer pricing; no conflict per se.

risks_watch: Jammu ramp-up depends on customer onboarding, customer audits and ROW country product approvals; management expects product approvals from various markets by the end of FY27.
Q1 is seasonally weak; management expects healthier season from Q2, and the 20%+ volume growth target depends on the H2 pickup.
Gross margin dipped 1-1.5 pts YoY on business mix; the full-year band is +/-2%.
Other expenses rose YoY and QoQ on higher operations and logistics costs; management did not quantify.
Management noted macro, political and geopolitical factors could change the business mix tailwind; it did not commit to sustaining the mix benefit.
Baddi new plot plan remains unfirmed; the next capex announcement is pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and reiterated FY27 guidance, but evasive on specifics: repeatedly deferred on Jammu margin, H2 growth and ex-Jammu margin, and avoided committing to figures beyond the 15-16% band. Management said challenges remain and that the 20% growth target is not easy.

financial_highlights.value: ~32% (management also cited ~30% on a rounded basis)

key_quotes: We have started financial year '27 on a strong note, delivering strong year-on-year growth of 34% and 33% in revenue and EBITDA respectively for the quarter.
So, our statement is that 20% volume growth vis -a-vis 20% sales growth.
So, challenges will be always there that we need to overcome from them.
